decisions.rationale: 'skin tumour' in the opening sentence refers to a broad family of tumour types rather than one defined disease, so it is a Disease Class.
'cancer' here is a general class of malignancies, not one specific defined disease. The guidelines retain the term cancer, so it is annotated as a Disease Class.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 - Disease Class; What NOT to Annotate §4 (cancer and tumor are retained)

decisions.rationale: 'colon cancers' refers to colon cancer as one defined disease entity (colorectal cancer) without further categorization in this context.
'adenomatous polyposis coli' names the APC gene-encoded protein, which is a molecular entity rather than a disease mention in this sentence.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 (only disease mentions are annotated)

decisions.rationale: 'APC' is the abbreviation of the protein/gene product, not a disease mention in this context.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 (only disease mentions are annotated)

decisions.rationale: 'colon and some other cancers' is a contiguous string referring to two separate disease mentions (colon cancers and other cancers), so it is annotated as one Composite Mention.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §2 - Composite Mention; Examples 7

decisions.rationale: 'skin tumours' is a broad family of tumour types in the transgenic mice context, which resemble pilomatricomas, so it is a Disease Class.
'pilomatricomas' names one specific defined disease entity with no further categorization.
'pilomatricomas' names one specific defined disease entity in the question about whether human pilomatricomas originate from hair matrix cells.
'skin tumour' in 'this common human skin tumour' is the same broad family-level term, so it is a Disease Class.
'tumour' is used as a modifier of the noun 'cells' in 'tumour cells', so it is annotated as a Modifier.
'pilomatricomas' names one specific defined disease entity in the statement that the tumours are derived from hair matrix cells.
'these tumours' refers anaphorically to the specific disease pilomatricomas in this context, so it is annotated as a Specific Disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 - Specific Disease; §4 (duplicate and contextual mentions)

decisions.rationale: 'human tumours' refers generally to the family of all human tumour types examined, not one specific disease.
'tumorigenesis' refers to the biological process of tumour formation, not to a disease, so it is excluded.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate §5 - Biological processes; Examples 9
